solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drug about to be taken by referee

indicators.note: whatever is taken by something is drawn inside it, so one piece ends up held within the other

parts.note: to referee a dispute is to mediate in it
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A sports official is about to be given some drug, perhaps a sedative after a rough match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug' reads as a noun but is the verb; 'referee' is also a verb, not the official.
explanation.definitionFit: To drug someone is to give them medicine or a substance, which is exactly what the verb means.

clue.text: New wine is essential

definitions.meaning: first meaning: grape juice before or during fermentation
second meaning: something you cannot do without

explanation.surface: A wine buff insists that drinking the new vintage is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: MUST is the winemaker's term for freshly pressed juice; 'a must' is something essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Must is unfermented grape juice in winemaking, and as a noun it also means an indispensable requirement.

clue.text: Cracks joke child is about to comprehend

indicators.note: to comprehend is literally to grasp or take in, so one piece goes inside another
about can mean turned round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: seed in the old biblical sense of offspring or descendants
cod is British slang for a hoax or joke, as in a cod accent

explanation.surface: A child is about to get a joke, cracking it at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Seed as 'child' is the old biblical sense of offspring. 'Cracks joke' looks like telling a joke, but 'Cracks' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracking a code or cipher means working out its hidden meaning, which is what decoding does.

clue.text: Joined Labour party

parts.note: surface reading: someone signed up to the British Labour Party
setter's reading: a party of labourers who are linked together by fetters

explanation.walkthrough: The capital L on Labour points to the British political party; read it as plain labour and the 'party' is a team of convicts working while shackled together.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain gang is a group of prisoners fettered to one another while doing hard manual work.

clue.text: Physician has many methods for treatment

indicators.note: something given treatment is worked on and altered, so these letters are processed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, fourteen letters

explanation.surface: A doctor has a whole range of ways to treat a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For treatment' sounds medical, matching the physician, but it tells you to rework the letters of the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sydenham was a seventeenth-century English doctor, often called the English Hippocrates.

clue.text: Old gentleman is major underworld figure

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
sir is the polite address for a gentleman
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly gent turns out to be a big gangland boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld figure' suggests a crime boss; here it is the ruler of the dead in mythology.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the ancient Egyptian god who ruled over the dead and judged souls in the afterlife.

clue.text: Lot and Samson lost it

definitions.note: a description of the answer rather than a synonym
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Philistines blinded Samson after capturing him

explanation.surface: Two Old Testament figures and something they each lost: Lot his wife, Samson his hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Lot looks like the biblical man, sitting next to Samson, but it is the ordinary word for a large amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially 'a sight' means a great deal, and Samson's eyes were put out, losing him his vision.

clue.text: Show likely to change again

parts.note: a meter or dial reads a value when it shows it
apt to do something means likely to do it

explanation.surface: A television programme that will probably be altered once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a noun, a programme, but works as the verb used of gauges and thermometers.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to modify or adjust, and the prefix makes it do so a second time.

clue.text: Means to see better performances

definitions.meaning: first meaning: glasses that correct vision
second meaning: impressive shows or displays

explanation.surface: A critic's aim is to watch finer productions on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one sentence about seeing good shows, but it splits after 'better' into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles are eyeglasses, and a spectacle is also a grand public show or display.

clue.text: Using pins, but not in a good way

definitions.text: Using pins, but not in a good way

parts.note: pins is British slang for legs, so using them means moving on foot
'in a bad way' is the idiom for being hurt or unwell

explanation.surface: Someone is misusing sewing pins, handling them badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Pins is British slang for legs; 'not in a good way' is the idiom for being in poor health, not a comment on technique. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes casualties who are hurt but still able to get about on foot without stretchers.

clue.text: Bones bend when set the wrong way

indicators.note: placed in the wrong direction means running backwards, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: an arc is a curve or bend
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Broken bones that are set badly will bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set the wrong way' sounds like a botched fracture repair but signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacrum is the triangular bone at the base of the spine, and the Latin plural names several of them.

clue.text: Poem about open country, also a drink

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
range is open grazing land, as in the American West
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pastoral poem about the countryside that also celebrates a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem wraps round both the country and the A, splitting after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweetened, often fizzy soft drink flavoured with orange juice.

clue.text: From study, observes characteristic area linking seas

parts.note: a den is a private study or workroom
to mark something is to notice or observe it
a trait is a distinguishing characteristic

explanation.surface: A scholar, working from his study, notes a typical stretch of water between oceans.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end; everything before it is three plain synonyms joined up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Denmark Strait is the channel between Greenland and Iceland connecting the Greenland Sea with the Atlantic Ocean.

clue.text: Expert wants nice spread in return

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a return on an investment is a profit

indicators.note: spread out means scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A skilled specialist expects a nice buffet spread as payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a buffet and 'return' like giving back, but one scrambles letters and the other is a financial gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone proficient is highly skilled and competent, as an expert in a field is.

clue.text: Tinkers with damaged cars, unfinished too

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a thing left unfinished lacks its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: also and too are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles about with wrecked cars and never completes the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinkers' reads as a verb, fiddling with engines; it is a plural noun, the British word for mischievous children.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a tinker is a playful name for a naughty child, much like a scamp or rogue.

clue.text: Relatively favourable

parts.note: surface reading: fairly good, on the positive side compared with others
setter's reading: favourable to one's relatives, giving family members jobs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' normally means comparatively; here it means 'towards relatives'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes nepotism, the practice of those in power showing favouritism to kin.

clue.text: Bird's split crest

parts.note: to part is to split or divide
a ridge is the crest of a hill or roof

explanation.surface: A bird has a divided crest of feathers on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', linking definition to wordplay, not a possessive; 'crest' means a ridge, not plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a plump game bird of fields and farmland.

clue.text: Tired of having standards?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: grew weary, lost energy
second meaning: decked with flags, which are also called standards

explanation.surface: Someone is fed up with having to live up to principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standards' suggests moral principles, but a standard is also a banner or flag.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to grow weak or weary, and something flagged carries banners.

clue.text: He fills it before take-off

parts.note: surface reading: a man filling up a fuel tank before a plane departs
setter's reading: He is the chemical symbol for helium, the lifting gas pumped into a craft

explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a pilot or mechanic; it is the symbol for helium, the gas that gives a dirigible its lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible or blimp is a lighter-than-air craft kept aloft by a gas-filled envelope.

clue.text: Conflict over uncooked food

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: raw food is uncooked
fare is food, as in simple fare

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out about serving raw food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as 'about the subject of' but turns the adjective round.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfare is armed fighting between nations or groups, a state of hostility.

clue.text: Generally free

definitions.meaning: second meaning: not captured, as an escaped prisoner is

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that look like a single phrase each define the answer independently.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in general when describing a population, and uncaught when describing a fugitive.

clue.text: Green cannot be rural, oddly

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so the letters fall into an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A paradox: something green, it seems, can't belong to the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' is the colour of fields, which makes 'rural' tempting as the answer's sense; it means environmentally friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: An activity with no net emissions of greenhouse gases is environmentally friendly, which is what green means politically.

clue.text: A bird you seldom will catch

indicators.note: what catches something holds it within, so the letters sit inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: found across the two words, after the first letter

explanation.surface: Bird-watching advice: this is a species you will rarely spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel is an old name for the blackbird, and the ring ousel is a related thrush of upland Britain.

clue.text: Bypass over motorway heading for tunnel

parts.note: O is the scorecard abbreviation for an over in cricket
the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, written with I standing in for the 1

indicators.note: the heading of something is its top, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A road plan: a bypass goes over the motorway, leading to a tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bypass' looks like a road but is the verb meaning skip; the M1 runs from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to skip it or leave it out, the sense of omitting.

clue.text: Old old man

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-president
old man is informal for a husband

explanation.surface: A very elderly fellow, old twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word looks like emphasis for great age; the first 'old' means former and 'old man' is slang for a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's former spouse is her past partner, her 'old man' from earlier times.

clue.text: In part of kitchen, superior variety of wheat

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

parts.note: the drum is the rotating part of a washing machine, which in Britain usually stands in the kitchen
U means upper-class or superior in British usage

explanation.surface: A cook keeps a premium type of wheat in a cupboard in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'upper-class' comes from a once-famous British essay on posh versus common speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Durum is the hard wheat species whose flour is milled into semolina for making pasta.

clue.text: Suggestion — request to refuse a drink

parts.note: a tip is a helpful suggestion

indicators.note: to refuse something is to turn it away, so letters are rejected and dropped

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request
the article taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a polite request to turn down an offered drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The request loses the single letter named by 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipple is an alcoholic drink, especially someone's favourite, as in 'what's your tipple?'

clue.text: Any of the following

parts.note: surface reading: a puzzle instruction pointing to the items listed below
setter's reading: one member of a group of supporters or devotees

explanation.walkthrough: As the final clue it pretends to point at the list beneath; 'following' is a noun meaning a body of supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter or follower of a cause, leader or faith is one of its devotees.
